description:
Hello, I am an Aerospace engineer with a love for Prognosis and Health Management (PHM) systems. I am also a beginner at Python so our team would need programmers.

Astronauts face severe health issues in space if not adequately catered for. We don't want this since they are there to represent all of mankind, bringing us a step closer to understanding our universe through their research.

Let's build a system to help keep them healthy throughout their mission.
summary:
Astronaut Health Monitoring and Management Platform

A visual, AI-powered health monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It enables astronauts to input tested vital signs, monitor physiological changes, and receive personalized health insights. The system processes submitted health data to identify potential health concerns and provides recommendations for health improvement, preventive care, and effective condition management. By supporting continuous health assessment and informed decision-making, the platform helps astronauts maintain optimal physical well-being, manage mission-related health risks, and respond promptly to emerging concerns. Ultimately, it promotes astronaut safety, operational readiness, and mission success throughout extended space exploration.
details:
What exactly does it do? - It monitors astronauts' health status over long-term space missions (i.e., a mission to Mars).

How does it work? - It guides astronauts in taking valuable vitals, assesses input, and provides feedback, i.e., guidance on treatments, health management, and improvement strategies.

What benefits does it have? - It helps preserve astronauts' health throughout long-term missions.

What do you hope to achieve? - A health monitoring software that enables astronauts' evaluate and act on their health status.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?- Languages: JavaScript (ES modules), HTML5, CSS3, SQL.

Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript single-page app with no framework, Chart.js for charts, hosted on Vercel.

Backend: Node.js 22 with Express, hosted on Render. PostgreSQL database on Neon.

NASA data: Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) RAD radiation measurements from the NASA Planetary Data System, and space-weather events from the NASA DONKI API.

Tools: Git and GitHub, Visual Studio Code, the Node.js built-in test runner, FFmpeg for the demo video.

Hardware: Standard laptops only. No sensors or custom hardware; all health entries are typed in by the user.
